raw_findings.message: Casting shares to uint128 silently truncates deposits that mint more than uint128 shares, while totalShares still increases by the full amount, leaving the depositor unable to withdraw the shares recorded in the vault.
Every deposit appends the depositor again, so distributeRewards credits that user's full current share balance once per entry and can make rewardsOwed exceed the ETH actually received.

Anyone can append arbitrarily many holder entries, including with deposits that mint zero shares, eventually making the owner-only reward distribution loop exceed the transaction gas limit and permanently preventing distributions.
sharePrice divides by totalShares without handling an empty vault, so calling it before the first deposit or after all shares are withdrawn always reverts.

The vault pays the withdrawing contract before burning its shares, allowing its callback to deposit against the temporarily reduced balance and unchanged share supply to obtain excess shares at other holders' expense.
Any caller can change feeRecipient and redirect future withdrawal fees because this setter has no owner authorization check.
Using tx.origin for authorization lets an owner be tricked into calling an intermediary that invokes this setter, allowing that intermediary to change the withdrawal fee.
The fee transfer's success value is ignored, so a rejecting fee recipient causes the withdrawal to proceed without collecting the fee and leaves that amount in the vault.
Unchecked subtraction lets transferFrom wrap a zero or insufficient allowance to a huge value, allowing callers to transfer tokens without the owner's required allowance.

raw_findings.message: Casting `shares` to `uint128` can truncate a large deposit's minted shares while `totalShares` is increased by the full amount, leaving the depositor unable to withdraw the unrecorded shares.

Every deposit adds another holder entry, so `distributeRewards` credits a repeat depositor's full current balance once per entry and can make `rewardsOwed` exceed the ETH held, causing `totalAssets` to underflow.
The payout calls the recipient before burning shares, allowing a recipient callback to deposit against the transient balance and mint excess shares that dilute other holders.
The reward loop processes every historical deposit entry, so users can make `distributeRewards` exceed the block gas limit by making enough small deposits and thereby prevent reward distributions.
Anyone can change `feeRecipient`, allowing an attacker to redirect future withdrawal fees to an address they control.
Authenticating with `tx.origin` lets a malicious contract called by the owner change the withdrawal fee without being the owner contract's direct caller.
The fee transfer's success value is ignored, so a reverting fee recipient can prevent the fee from being paid while the withdrawal proceeds as if it had been paid.
The unchecked subtraction wraps when `amount` exceeds the approved allowance, allowing any spender to call `transferFrom` and drain a holder's tokens if that holder has sufficient balance.

raw_findings.message: Every deposit appends another holder entry, so repeated deposits can grow `holders` until `distributeRewards` runs out of gas and rewards can no longer be distributed.
Calling `distributeRewards` before any shares exist divides by zero and reverts, so the owner cannot fund rewards before the first deposit.

Because `holders` contains duplicate addresses, the loop credits each repeated holder entry with their full current shares, allowing a depositor to make `rewardsOwed` exceed the ETH actually supplied for rewards.
Anyone can replace `feeRecipient`, allowing an attacker to redirect fees from future withdrawals to themselves.
Checking `tx.origin` lets a contract called by the owner change the withdrawal fee without being the owner, so a phishing interaction can set the fee up to its maximum.
The fee transfer's success value is ignored, so a rejecting fee recipient leaves the fee in the vault while withdrawals proceed as if it was paid.
The unchecked subtraction wraps when `amount` exceeds the allowance, allowing anyone to use `transferFrom` to take tokens from an address with sufficient balance and insufficient approval.
Transfers to the zero address are allowed, permanently locking tokens there while leaving them included in `totalSupply`.
